adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 117.2. The target week has a price increase to $12.21 (+3.7%) with no events. The recent week (2026-04-06) sold 128 units at the same price, vs baseline 117.2 — a 9.2% uplift, but this is likely noise (ordinary week noise is ±33%). The Easter week (2026-03-30) at the same price sold 146 units (x1.25 vs baseline), but was a holiday. Past promotions show a noise-adjusted uplift of x1.43, but this is a price increase, not a discount. Price hikes typically reduce demand. The post-promotion effect is x0.82, but no promotion preceded this week. No evidence of demand lift from price, and a 3.7% increase is likely to depress sales. The classical model suggests no uplift, which is correct. Adjust down modestly due to price increase, with uncertainty.

  median 117.2 | 5%-95%: 52.1 - 200.3 | 10%-90%: 56.5 - 165.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-33% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
